summary: We reviewed local reports and organizational information to understand the gap.

next_step.summary: Use AI to review new local evidence when it becomes available, retaining sources and distinguishing proposals from operating services.

open_questions: What new local evidence changes the starting picture?

title: Investigate barriers to fostering and adoption
summary: We're investigating the housing, cost, veterinary, and care constraints that keep willing people from helping.

next_step.title: Test the initial barrier map
next_step.summary: Use responder accounts and firsthand evidence to identify which barriers matter most locally and what would make helping practical.

open_questions: Which barriers most often prevent willing Stockton residents from fostering or adopting?
How do street outreach, the proposed Canine Campus, veterinary care, and pet-inclusive housing fit together?
Where could AI or automation reduce a practical burden, and how would we test whether it helps?

initial_map.summary: AI organized public evidence into an initial barrier map. Fieldwork will test and refine it.

threads.title: Limited foster and indoor care space
threads.summary: Public evidence points to constrained shelter and placement capacity. Suitable temporary care and recovery space is an initial barrier to investigate.
open_questions: What suitable foster or recovery space is missing?
Which constraints could the proposed Canine Campus address, and which would remain?

threads.title: Veterinary costs and access
threads.summary: Public evidence identifies veterinary access and sterilization capacity as pressures. Costs, appointments, transport, and recovery care need local investigation.
open_questions: Where do cost or appointment availability block care or placement?
What happens between a spay/neuter appointment and a safe recovery placement?

threads.title: Housing and shelter restrictions
threads.summary: Public-source framing identifies housing constraints, while the Safe Grounds proposal connects shelter access with companion animals. Specific local restrictions and their effects remain to be verified.
open_questions: Which housing or shelter rules prevent people and dogs from staying together?
How does proposed pet-inclusive housing relate to the Canine Campus?

threads.title: Time and care commitments
threads.summary: Crossover’s public-source framing identifies time and care logistics as potential barriers. Training, transport, and backup-care burdens are questions for firsthand investigation.
open_questions: What time, training, transport, or backup support would make fostering practical?
Which burdens could shared support or automation reduce?

threads.title: Connecting willing people with opportunities
threads.summary: Public information lists participation routes. Whether unclear roles, application friction, or matching prevent participation is a hypothesis to test, not an established local finding.
open_questions: Can a willing person find a suitable role and get started?
Where does onboarding or matching stall, if it does?

title: Direct conversations and field visits
summary: We're contacting local responders and trying ways to help firsthand.

next_step.title: Try Doggie Day Out
next_step.summary: Check participation requirements and apply or register as needed.

open_questions: What work is most useful to responders?
What prevents willing people from participating?
